How we handle images and QR results

Effective October 28, 2026

QR Image Reader decodes QR codes on your device. We do not run a decoding server or receive, sell, or share your images, QR results, or browsing history. The extension uses no ads, analytics, or remotely executed scripts.

What is processed on your device

When you scan from the image menu, the extension reads the selected image, its address, and its position. If the page blocks pixel access, Chrome may provide an in-memory screenshot. The extension immediately crops it to the visible part of the selected image and temporarily stores only the crop. Images you select, drop, or paste are also decoded on your device.

Temporary storage and deletion

Images captured from the context menu and their addresses are temporarily stored in the browser’s local IndexedDB and are not synced. Closing the result window or tab, or choosing “Clear,” deletes the associated task. Up to 12 tasks are kept. Leftover tasks expire after 30 minutes and are removed during a subsequent cleanup. Restarting Chrome also clears leftover tasks.

Local files and decoded results stay in the open window’s memory. Under “Privacy and help,” you can clear all temporary images. Choose “Clear” in an open window to remove what it is showing. Chrome removes extension storage when you uninstall it.

When the extension uses the network

The extension requests the selected image from its website only when you choose “Read original.” Chrome may ask for website access and include that site’s existing sign-in cookies. The extension does not read, export, or save cookie values. The image website handles normal request information under its own policy. HTTP requests lack HTTPS encryption; you can save or capture the image and scan it locally instead.

Chrome keeps granted website access until you revoke it in the extension or in Chrome’s extension details. A failed scan does not automatically make an authenticated request. The extension visits an HTTP(S) address in a result only when you choose “Open link.”

Clipboard and Incognito

The extension reads an image only when you paste it, and writes a result to the clipboard only when you choose to copy it. It does not read the clipboard in the background, request camera or browsing history access, or run in Incognito.

Why these permissions are used

contextMenus adds the image menu. activeTab allows temporary access to the current tab after you use the extension. scripting reads the selected image element when needed. Optional HTTP(S) site access applies to the image’s site when you choose “Read original.”

Contact and policy updates

devsaddle@gmail.com

If you contact support, your email service and the recipient’s mailbox process your message. Please do not send passwords, private QR codes, or other unnecessary information.

This website is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub handles ordinary access logs under its own privacy policy. This website does not set cookies or use analytics scripts or forms. The site matches your preferred language in your browser. If you choose a language manually, only that choice is stored in this browser. Choose “Follow browser” to clear it.

If our data handling changes, we will update this policy and explain the changes in the extension.
